## About this course

Clinical staff make decisions every day that research could improve, but few have been taught how to turn a bedside uncertainty into a published study. Over eight weeks, with one 3-hour online session every Saturday evening (19:30–22:30), this course walks the whole road of research: asking a good question, finding and reading the evidence, choosing a design, recognising bias, collecting and analysing data, protecting participants, writing the paper and getting it published.

- **Slow and visual.** Built for participants with no research background: pictures first, a "check your understanding" every 20 minutes, no formulas beyond a 2×2 table, and extra slides at the end of each session for anyone who wants to read further at home.
- **Online, one class.** You join from home. There are no groups or breakout rooms: every exercise is done by the whole class together, with polls and the chat.
- **The whole road in one course.** Weeks 1–4 build understanding and design skills; Weeks 5–8 read the results of a realistic simulated dataset (FLUID-ICU, 620 ICU patients) through live instructor demos in R, and each participant writes the Results section of a paper from them.
- **Level 1 of three.** This course is Level 1. Level 2 is a separate hands-on course in R for those who want to run analyses themselves (in preparation). Level 3 covers advanced, specialised methods on request. See [Course levels](levels.qmd).
- **One running example:** fluids in septic shock. The example is followed through question and search, design, analysis, write-up and publication, and appraised through two real papers.

## Two individual products

```{=html}
<div class="cards2"><div><h4>1 · A research proposal</h4><p>On your <strong>own clinical question</strong> from your department, with a publication plan. Each part is shown live on the running example and you write your own as homework. Everyone <strong>submits it in Session 8</strong>; about 5 volunteers also present it (6 minutes + 2 minutes feedback).</p></div><div><h4>2 · A Results section</h4><p>From the course dataset <strong>FLUID-ICU</strong>: at the end of Session 6 you choose one of the five questions (Q1 to Q5). We give you the results pack, and you write a <strong>submission-ready Results section</strong> with a working title, Table 1 and a main table or figure. The other sections are optional. It is due by 23:59 on the day of Session 8. A classmate <strong>peer reviews</strong> it (by 2 January 2027), and you send your revision and response by 30 January 2027.</p></div></div>
```

## Who it is for

**Health professionals (doctors, nurses, etc.)**, about 30 participants per class, joining online from home. No research or statistics background is assumed, and no software is needed: the trainers run the analyses and you learn to read, interpret and write them up. You need a computer with a stable internet connection, camera and microphone.

## How to start

- Request your free [access code](access.qmd) (once per browser).
- **Before Session 1, read the [proposal brief](proposal-brief.qmd).** It is the one document to read before the course. It comes by email with the proposal template, the presentation guide and the proposal rubric (table below).
- Then see [Session 1](session1.qmd): the two papers, the exercise sheet and the online set-up. Look at the [schedule](schedule.qmd).
- Each session page has the agenda, the slides, the exercise sheet and what to prepare.
